text:
I read the pinned IDURAR source and I am proposing **8 tools** for the authenticated back office: customers, invoices, payments.

- `find_customers` — look a company up before billing it
- `create_customer` — put a new client on file
- `find_invoices` — filter by unpaid, status, or customer
- `get_invoice` — line items and the exact balance due
- `create_invoice` — draft a bill for work done
- `prepare_invoice_payment` — quote a payment, write nothing
- `confirm_invoice_payment` — record it, token-gated
- `get_finance_summary` — total invoiced and outstanding

Three calls worth your attention.

**No journey template matches** this app — it is an internal ERP, not a shop, booking site or lead funnel. I instantiated from its own routes rather than forcing the nearest category.

**No `ask_site`** — there is no visitor-facing content here to answer from, and I will not invent a content bundle.

**Payment is split in two.** This build’s own Record Payment form cannot be submitted: its required Payment Mode field reads a backend entity that does not exist. So a prepare/confirm token pair is the safety boundary instead of a UI handoff.

I left out emailing invoices and deleting records — irreversible, no undo.

Pick the tools to build, request one I missed, leave a note, then submit.

All **8 tools** are built and the static check is green: the production build compiles every module and all eight tool names appear in the bundle.

Two things I hit while building, both worth a look:

- **This build’s own write forms are dead ends.** The invoice form’s tax selector and the payment form’s Payment Mode selector both read backend entities (`taxes`, `paymentMode`) that do not exist here, and both fields are required — so neither form can be submitted in the UI, while the API routes behind them work fine. The tools go through the app’s redux layer and do complete these journeys.
- **`find_invoices` filters on one field at a time.** The list endpoint takes a single filter/equal pair, exactly as the app’s own table does. Rather than quietly dropping one filter, the tool refuses the combination and tells the caller to filter by one and read the other off the returned rows.

Also worth confirming: the repo’s `.eslintrc.js` is broken upstream (CommonJS config in a `"type": "module"` package), so `npm run lint` fails on a clean checkout too. I used the production build as the static check instead and left the config alone.

Read the code on any card. Leave feedback on anything you want changed, or approve to run the full browser verification and open the PR.
